answers.text: Simple — three lines, always the same order: drop-off time, pallet count, any damage noted. Every time, no exceptions.
I'd just make a list of this week's calls with who was contacted and why.
The finish time doesn't add up — 8am start, six-hour job, but it says finishing early afternoon the next day. Worth checking which date is right.
The 96 to 118 jump looks bigger than a 20% rise to me. And 9 late out of 118 isn't quite 92% either — I'd get both numbers checked.
Output 2, definitely — you can see the actual ticket counts behind the 88%. Output 1 gives you nothing to check.
Email 2 — it's got the actual volume numbers in it. Email 1 doesn't even say what 'current volumes' means, so there's nothing to check it against.
1. No. 2. Yes. 3. Yes, it's just a draft, should be fine. 4. No. 5. No.
I'd redact the hourly rates before pasting anything in, and I'd be careful with the non-disclosure clause too since it names both companies.
I'd have someone cross-check the stock counts against the system before the monthly summary goes out.
